A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The revised proofs and removal of v1's checklist can be reliably distinguished from retained content.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 report original experiments on synthetic constrained linear regression and vertical federated regression using the mushrooms dataset.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 retain these original experimental results.

M1.justification: Theorem 1 revises Algorithm 2's prescribed momentum and step-size parameters: tau uses 44 max{1+kappa_f,6} instead of 60 max{1+kappa_f,8}, and eta uses 6mu_f instead of 8mu_f. The APAPC updates and Chebyshev procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic constrained linear-regression task and mushrooms-based vertical federated regression. No dataset, domain, or empirical test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tracking-ADMM and DPMM remain the evaluated comparators in both experiments and both figures. Table 1's literature comparison is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same Gaussian data generation, graph settings, dimensions, sample counts, regularization, and evaluation against gradient calls, matrix multiplications, and communications. The theorem-level parameter revisions are not documented as changes to the experiments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports additional ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or empirical error analyses. The expanded appendix contains theoretical arguments rather than supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: V1's checklist explicitly states that no error bars are included because the algorithms are deterministic; v2 removes this disclosure. The figures remain without uncertainty estimates, and neither version supplies seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 retain identical plotted convergence results, comparator rankings, and experimental conditions. Section 6's finding that the proposed algorithm has the steepest convergence slopes is unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 replaces memory sets with linear spans, and Theorem 2 now asserts all three lower bounds for one hard instance instead of separating the gradient-bound instance. Appendix B revises the construction and adds a weighted-graph argument, Lemmas 6–7, and an explicit gradient-hard extension. Appendix A corrects a missing factor n in Lemma 2's proof and tightens the constants used in Theorem 1.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution discussion retain the same claims of a first-order, linearly convergent method for general affine coupled constraints and optimal complexity matching lower bounds. The stronger formal statement of Theorem 2 does not reframe these headline contributions.

C2.justification: The explanation of convergence slopes through communication-versus-gradient costs is retained. The removed checklist's limitations statement merely repeats smoothness, strong convexity, and gossip-matrix assumptions that remain in Section 3.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly derives the revised algorithm parameters. Removing the checklist also removes v1's statement that code is provided in supplementary material; the PDFs do not establish that the code itself became unavailable. Hardware and experimental implementation disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B gives Kovalev et al. (2021) a more explicit role in the lower-bound construction and minimizer argument, while retaining Scaman et al. (2017) for the graph construction. Both works were already cited; the bibliography and broader related-work positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. V2 adds explanatory definitions, reorganizes Appendix B into more focused subsections, removes the submission checklist, and changes author order. These are localized editorial and structural changes.

P2.justification: Table 1, Figures 1–2, and the six algorithm displays retain their designs. Expanded equations and prose produce local reflow, including changes around Proposition 1, Figure 1, and the start of the references, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix A repairs the missing n factor and makes parameter choices clearer, while Appendix B expands previously sketched arguments. However, the new Lemma 6 derivation drops a factor of three when converting 3mu/(L−mu)=mu_A mu_f/(L_A L_f) into L/mu. This inconsistency affects the central lower-bound argument accompanying the strengthened Theorem 2. These benefits and proof concerns leave the net quality change uncertain.
